samasa.type: karmadhāraya (avadhāraṇa-pūrvapada: the first member identifies the form)
samasa.literal: by the form that is compassion
samasa.sense: as compassion, in the shape of compassion
samasa.alt: Also read as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, दयायाः रूपम् ‘the form of compassion’. The karmadhāraya fits better: the Goddess is not said to own a form belonging to compassion but to be present as compassion itself.

morph.note: दया is a feminine noun in -ā from √दय् (bhvādi, 1Ā, दयते ‘to pity, to share out’): compassion, the impulse to relieve another’s suffering.
Past passive participle of सम् + √स्था, as in 5.35-37: ‘(who) abides’, with अस्ति understood.

mantras.anvaya: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु दयारूपेण संस्थिता (अस्ति), तस्यै नमः (अस्तु), तस्यै नमः, तस्यै नमः, नमः नमः।
mantras.anvaya_en: The relative clause (या … संस्थिता) and its correlative (तस्यै), as in 5.35-37.
mantras.lit: The Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of compassion — homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.
mantras.tr: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as compassion: salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her — salutation again and again.
mantras.tr_note: ‘As’ renders the instrumental -रूपेण ‘in the form of’; ‘again and again’ renders the doubled नमो नमः.

comm.t: The Goddess is named as compassion (दया), present in every creature that pities another.

The gods’ hymn in chapter 4 says she sends her weapons against enemies so that, purified by them, even they may reach the higher worlds (4.19), and concludes: ‘thus is compassion shown by you even to enemies’ (4.21: वैरिष्वपि प्रकटितैव दया त्वयेत्थम्). Compassion in the heart and ruthlessness in battle are found together in her alone (4.22).
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has दयामूर्तिः ‘embodiment of compassion’ as name 581 — a compound rather than the bare word, but the same idea.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (avadhāraṇa-pūrvapada: the first member identifies the form)
samasa.literal: by the form that is contentment
samasa.sense: as contentment, in the shape of contentment
samasa.alt: Also read as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, तुष्टेः रूपम् ‘the form of contentment’. The karmadhāraya fits better: the Goddess is not said to own a form belonging to contentment but to be present as contentment itself.

morph.note: तुष्टि is an action noun from √तुष् ‘to be pleased, satisfied’ (divādi, 4P, तुष्यति) with -ति (क्तिन्); the ṣ of the root turns the t of the suffix to ṭ (ष्टुना ष्टुः, 8.4.41).
Past passive participle of सम् + √स्था, as in 5.35-37: ‘(who) abides’, with अस्ति understood.

mantras.anvaya: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु तुष्टिरूपेण संस्थिता (अस्ति), तस्यै नमः (अस्तु), तस्यै नमः, तस्यै नमः, नमः नमः।
mantras.anvaya_en: The relative clause (या … संस्थिता) and its correlative (तस्यै), as in 5.35-37.
mantras.lit: The Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of contentment — homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.
mantras.tr: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as contentment: salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her — salutation again and again.
mantras.tr_note: ‘As’ renders the instrumental -रूपेण ‘in the form of’; ‘again and again’ renders the doubled नमो नमः.

comm.t: The Goddess is named as contentment (तुष्टि): the satisfaction that rests in what one has.
Contentment answers the thirst of 5.35-37: the hymn names her both as the craving that drives a creature and as the satisfaction that stills it. Brahmā’s hymn already named her तुष्टिः (1.80).
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has तुष्टिः as name 443, the first of a run of such qualities (443–449).

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (avadhāraṇa-pūrvapada: the first member identifies the form)
samasa.literal: by the form that is the mother
samasa.alt: Also read as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, मातुः रूपम् ‘the form of the mother’. The karmadhāraya fits better: the Goddess is not said to own a form belonging to the mother but to be present as the mother itself.

morph.note: मातृ is an ṛ-stem noun of relationship (nom. sg. माता, gen. मातुः), traditionally connected with √मा ‘to measure, to form’. In a compound the bare stem मातृ stands; the vigraha uses the nominative माता.
Past passive participle of सम् + √स्था, as in 5.35-37: ‘(who) abides’, with अस्ति understood.

mantras.anvaya: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु मातृरूपेण संस्थिता (अस्ति), तस्यै नमः (अस्तु), तस्यै नमः, तस्यै नमः, नमः नमः।
mantras.anvaya_en: The relative clause (या … संस्थिता) and its correlative (तस्यै), as in 5.35-37.
mantras.lit: The Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of the mother — homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.
mantras.tr: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as mother: salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her — salutation again and again.
mantras.tr_note: ‘As’ renders the instrumental -रूपेण ‘in the form of’; ‘again and again’ renders the doubled नमो नमः.

comm.t: The Goddess is named as the mother present in all beings: motherhood itself, in every creature that bears and nourishes young.

The word is singular here: not a group of goddesses but the motherhood in each being. In chapter 8 the plural Mātṛs, the Mothers, will come forth from the gods’ own powers to fight beside her (8.12–14); the tradition sees them as her emanations.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) opens with श्रीमाता (name 1) and has माता as name 457. The two texts remain separate works.
A modern reflection: the care of any mother for any child is named here as a form of the Goddess, not merely a picture of her.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (avadhāraṇa-pūrvapada: the first member identifies the form)
samasa.literal: by the form that is error
samasa.sense: as error, in the shape of error
samasa.alt: Also read as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, भ्रान्तेः रूपम् ‘the form of error’. The karmadhāraya fits better: the Goddess is not said to own a form belonging to error but to be present as error itself.

morph.note: भ्रान्ति is an action noun from √भ्रम् ‘to wander, whirl’ (divādi 4P भ्राम्यति; also bhvādi 1P भ्रमति) with -ति (क्तिन्), the vowel lengthened as in शान्ति: a wandering, hence confusion, error, delusion.
Past passive participle of सम् + √स्था, as in 5.35-37: ‘(who) abides’, with अस्ति understood.

mantras.anvaya: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु भ्रान्तिरूपेण संस्थिता (अस्ति), तस्यै नमः (अस्तु), तस्यै नमः, तस्यै नमः, नमः नमः।
mantras.anvaya_en: The relative clause (या … संस्थिता) and its correlative (तस्यै), as in 5.35-37.
mantras.lit: The Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of error — homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.
mantras.tr: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as delusion: salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her — salutation again and again.
mantras.tr_note: ‘As’ renders the instrumental -रूपेण ‘in the form of’; ‘delusion’ is chosen for भ्रान्ति (lit. ‘wandering, error’) because of the link with Mahāmāyā’s मोह in 1.55–56; ‘again and again’ renders नमो नमः.

comm.t: The last name of the yā devī series is error, delusion (भ्रान्ति): the confusion that takes one thing for another.

The series ends on its hardest case. Medhas taught that this Goddess, as Mahāmāyā, forcibly draws even the minds of the wise into delusion (1.55–56: ज्ञानिनामपि चेतांसि … बलादाकृष्य मोहाय महामाया प्रयच्छति) and is also the cause of release (1.57–58). To bow to her as delusion is to acknowledge that the power that confuses is hers, and so is the power to free.
A modern reflection: error is not praised; it is placed under the same sovereignty as knowledge. That is the ground for hoping that error can be undone.
